claims.title: Foundation of Massalia (Marseille)
claims.summary: Greek colonists from Phocaea establish a trading port — the oldest city in France.

claims.summary: The first Frankish king to adopt Catholic Christianity, aligning crown and Church.

claims.title: Charlemagne crowned Emperor
claims.summary: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne in Rome, reviving the Western imperial title.

claims.title: Rollo and the Viking grant of Normandy
claims.summary: Around 911 the West Frankish king Charles the Simple granted the Viking leader Rollo lands around Rouen in return for baptism and the defence of the Seine, the beginning of the duchy whose rulers conquered England in 1066.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-911-rollo-and-the-viking-grant-of-normandy, claim TL:FRA:event:911:rollo-and-the-viking-grant-of-normandy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Beginning of the Capetian dynasty and the long consolidation of the French crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-987-hugh-capet-elected-king, claim TL:FRA:event:987:hugh-capet-elected-king, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hundred Years' War begins
claims.summary: A dynastic struggle with England that would last until 1453 and forge French identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1337-hundred-years-war-begins, claim TL:FRA:event:1337:hundred-years-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joan of Arc at Orléans
claims.summary: Joan lifts the siege of Orléans, reversing English fortunes; she is executed in 1431.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1429-joan-of-arc-at-orleans, claim TL:FRA:event:1429:joan-of-arc-at-orleans, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Edict of Nantes
claims.summary: Henry IV grants toleration to Protestants, ending the Wars of Religion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1598-edict-of-nantes, claim TL:FRA:event:1598:edict-of-nantes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Louis XIV
claims.summary: Absolutism and the court of Versailles make France the dominant power in Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1643-reign-of-louis-xiv, claim TL:FRA:event:1643:reign-of-louis-xiv, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cayenne settled
claims.summary: A Rouen company's expedition under Charles Poncet de Brétigny buys the hill at the mouth of the Cayenne river from a local leader, Cépérou, and builds a fort. Dutch and English forces take the town several times before France regains it for good in 1664.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1643-cayenne-settled, claim TL:FRA:event:1643:cayenne-settled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Utrecht names the “Japoc or Vincent Pinson”
claims.summary: Article 8 fixes the France–Portugal frontier in Guiana on a river of that name. Brazil later argued it was the Oyapock and France that it was the Araguari, a disagreement settled by arbitration in 1900.

sources.label: Arbitral award on the Brazil/French Guiana boundary, 1 December 1900
sources.publisher: United Nations, Reports of International Arbitral Awards vol. XXVIII

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1713-treaty-of-utrecht-names-the-japoc-or-vincent, claim TL:FRA:event:1713:treaty-of-utrecht-names-the-japoc-or-vincent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kourou expedition
claims.summary: After the Treaty of Paris, France sends thousands of settlers to the Kourou coast in French Guiana with little prepared for them. Disease kills a large share of them within about two years; sources differ on the totals.

sources.label: Kourou, 1763: le dernier rêve de l’Amérique française (review)
Welcome to Kourou, Colony of Death

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1763-the-kourou-expedition, claim TL:FRA:event:1763:the-kourou-expedition, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Storming of the Bastille
claims.summary: The opening act of the French Revolution; later France's national day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1789-storming-of-the-bastille, claim TL:FRA:event:1789:storming-of-the-bastille, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man
claims.summary: Proclaims liberty, equality and popular sovereignty — a founding text of modern democracy.

sources.label: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1789-declaration-of-the-rights-of-man, claim TL:FRA:event:1789:declaration-of-the-rights-of-man, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Napoleon crowned Emperor
claims.summary: Bonaparte founds the First Empire and exports the Napoleonic Code across Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1804-napoleon-crowned-emperor, claim TL:FRA:event:1804:napoleon-crowned-emperor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Napoleon's final defeat ends the Empire and the Napoleonic Wars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1815-battle-of-waterloo, claim TL:FRA:event:1815:battle-of-waterloo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Penal colonies in French Guiana
claims.summary: From 1852 France sends convicts to penal camps in French Guiana, including the Îles du Salut. A decree of 1938 ends transportation; the last return convoy leaves in 1953. The Archives nationales d’outre-mer database covers nearly 100,000 convicts sent to French Guiana or New Caledonia between 1852 and 1953.

sources.label: Base des bagnards (Archives nationales d’outre-mer), announcement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1852-penal-colonies-in-french-guiana, claim TL:FRA:event:1852:penal-colonies-in-french-guiana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russian arbitration on the Maroni frontier
claims.summary: Emperor Alexander III of Russia, as arbitrator, rules that the Awa is the border river between French Guiana and Suriname; land upstream of its confluence with the Tapanahoni goes to the Netherlands. The award does not settle every question on the Suriname frontier.

sources.label: Award on the France/Netherlands boundary in Guiana, 25 May 1891
sources.publisher: United Nations, Reports of International Arbitral Awards vol. XXVIII

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1891-russian-arbitration-on-the-maroni-frontier, claim TL:FRA:event:1891:russian-arbitration-on-the-maroni-frontier, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dreyfus held on Devil’s Island
claims.summary: Captain Alfred Dreyfus, convicted of treason in 1894, is transferred in April 1895 to Devil’s Island off French Guiana to serve his sentence. He leaves the island in 1899; the Court of Cassation declares him innocent in 1906.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1895-dreyfus-held-on-devil-s-island, claim TL:FRA:event:1895:dreyfus-held-on-devil-s-island, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Swiss arbitration fixes the Brazil–French Guiana border
claims.summary: The Swiss Federal Council rules at Bern that the “Japoc or Vincent Pinson” of the Treaty of Utrecht is the Oyapock, as Brazil had argued, not the Araguari as France had. The border follows the Oyapock and, inland, the Tumuc-Humac watershed.

sources.label: Arbitral award on the Brazil/French Guiana boundary, 1 December 1900
sources.publisher: United Nations, Reports of International Arbitral Awards vol. XXVIII

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1900-swiss-arbitration-fixes-the-brazil-french, claim TL:FRA:event:1900:swiss-arbitration-fixes-the-brazil-french, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Separation of Church and State
claims.summary: The 1905 law establishes laïcité — France's distinctive secularism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1905-separation-of-church-and-state, claim TL:FRA:event:1905:separation-of-church-and-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberation of Paris
claims.summary: Allied and Free French forces liberate Paris after four years of occupation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1944-liberation-of-paris, claim TL:FRA:event:1944:liberation-of-paris, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French Guiana becomes a département
claims.summary: A law of 19 March 1946, championed by deputies including Aimé Césaire and French Guiana’s Gaston Monnerville, makes Martinique, Guadeloupe, Réunion and French Guiana départements of France.

sources.label: 80 ans de la loi du 19 mars 1946

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1946-french-guiana-becomes-a-departement, claim TL:FRA:event:1946:french-guiana-becomes-a-departement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fifth Republic founded
claims.summary: De Gaulle's new constitution creates the strong presidency that governs France today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1958-fifth-republic-founded, claim TL:FRA:event:1958:fifth-republic-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding member of the EEC
claims.summary: France signs the Treaty of Rome, beginning European integration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1957-founding-member-of-the-eec, claim TL:FRA:event:1957:founding-member-of-the-eec, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Guiana Space Centre
claims.summary: On 14 April 1964 Prime Minister Georges Pompidou announces French Guiana as the site of France’s new space centre, chosen from fourteen sites studied; a Véronique sounding rocket launched on 9 April 1968 makes it operational. The first Ariane flies from it in 1979.

sources.label: CSG at 50: half a century of Europe’s Spaceport

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-1964-guiana-space-centre, claim TL:FRA:event:1964:guiana-space-centre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The euro in French Guiana
claims.summary: French Guiana, a département of France, uses the euro; the Banque de France’s subsidiary IEDOM acts as its central-bank delegate in overseas territories whose currency is the euro.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-2002-the-euro-in-french-guiana, claim TL:FRA:event:2002:the-euro-in-french-guiana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French Guiana an EU outermost region
claims.summary: Article 349 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union names French Guiana among the outermost regions, whose remoteness justifies specific measures in the application of EU law there. It is one of nine such regions.

sources.label: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Article 349
Outermost regions
sources.publisher: European Commission, Regional and Urban Policy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-2009-french-guiana-an-eu-outermost-region, claim TL:FRA:event:2009:french-guiana-an-eu-outermost-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oyapock bridge opens
claims.summary: The bridge across the Oyapock between Saint-Georges-de-l’Oyapock and Oiapoque, finished in 2011, opens in 2017. France and Brazil share a border of more than 730 km, which the Sénat describes as France’s longest land border.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of France: From the forests of Gaul to the Fifth Republic", terralore.co/country/FRA/chronicle#ev-2017-oyapock-bridge-opens, claim TL:FRA:event:2017:oyapock-bridge-opens, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
